title: Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences: Explicit and Recursive Formulas
seo_title: Algebra 1 Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences Worksheets: Explicit and Recursive Formulas (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 sequences worksheets (F-BF.A.2, F-IF.A.3): arithmetic or geometric, explicit formulas a(n) = a(1) + d(n − 1) and a(n) = a(1) · r^(n − 1), recursive formulas, common ratios and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Arithmetic: add d each time, aₙ = a₁ + d(n − 1). Geometric: multiply by r, aₙ = a₁ · rⁿ⁻¹.
key_sub: A recursive formula uses the term before; an explicit formula jumps straight to any term.
body_html:
How it works

In an arithmetic sequence you add the same number each time (the common difference). Its nth term is dn + c, where d is the difference.

In a geometric sequence you multiply by the same number each time (the common ratio). Find the ratio by dividing a term by the term before. Square, cube, triangular and Fibonacci numbers are other special sequences.

Example

Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, …

The difference is 3, so start with 3n: 3, 6, 9, 12.

Each term is 2 more.

Answer: 3n + 2

Example

Find the next term of 3, 6, 12, 24, …

The ratio is 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

24 × 2.

Answer: 48

Example

Is 50 in the sequence 3n + 2?

3n + 2 = 50 gives 3n = 48, n = 16.

Answer: Yes, the 16th term

Common mistakes

  • Writing n + 3 for a difference of 3. It should be 3n.
  • Using the first term as the constant: 5, 8, 11, … is 3n + 2, not 3n + 5.
  • Adding the ratio instead of multiplying in a geometric sequence.
  • Calling square numbers arithmetic. Their differences are 3, 5, 7, … which are not equal.

faq.q: What is the difference between arithmetic and geometric sequences?
faq.a: In an arithmetic sequence you add the same amount each time. In a geometric sequence you multiply by the same amount each time.

faq.q: How do I find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?
faq.a: Find the common difference d and write dn. Then compare dn with the sequence to find the number to add or subtract.

faq.q: How do I find the common ratio?
faq.a: Divide any term by the term before it. For 3, 12, 48, … the ratio is 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

faq.q: What is the difference between a recursive and an explicit formula?
faq.a: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before. An explicit formula gives any term directly from n.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, 25, 125, 625, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 625 × 5 = 3,125.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 18, 17, 16, 15, 14, …
items.e: The difference is always −1, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 3, 10, 17, 24, 31, …
items.e: The difference is always 7, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 2, 6, 18, 54, 162, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 3, so it is geometric.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 2, so it is geometric.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, 12, 36, 108, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 3 each time. 108 × 3 = 324.

items.q: What is the next term? 11, 12, 13, 14, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: add 1 each time. 14 + 1 = 15.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 17, 20, 23, 26, 29, …
items.e: The difference is always 3, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 12, 48, 192, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 192 × 4 = 768.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 19, 25, 31, 37, 43, …
items.e: The difference is always 6, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 18, 13, 8, 3, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 5 each time. 3 − 5 = −2.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, −12, 36, −108, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by −3 each time. −108 × (−3) = 324.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, …
items.e: The differences change (4, 5, 6, 7) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? −4, −10, −16, −22, −28, …
items.e: The difference is always −6, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, 20, 100, 500, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 500 × 5 = 2,500.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, 15, 45, 135, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 3 each time. 135 × 3 = 405.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 15, 75, 375, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 375 × 5 = 1,875.

items.q: What is the next term? 1, 3, 9, 27, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 3 each time. 27 × 3 = 81.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, −9, 27, −81, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by −3 each time. −81 × (−3) = 243.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 2, so it is geometric.

sets.title: The nth term of arithmetic sequences

items.q: What is the nth term of 3, 8, 13, 18, …?
items.e: The difference is 5, so start with 5n. The 1st term of 5n is 5; to get 3, subtract 2. 5n − 2.

items.q: What is the nth term of 3, 9, 15, 21, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get 3, subtract 3. 6n − 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of −9, −8, −7, −6, …?
items.e: The difference is 1, so start with n. The 1st term of n is 1; to get −9, subtract 10. n − 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of −11, −12, −13, −14, …?
items.e: The difference is −1, so start with −n. The 1st term of −n is −1; to get −11, subtract 10. −n − 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of 0, −1, −2, −3, …?
items.e: The difference is −1, so start with −n. The 1st term of −n is −1; to get 0, add 1. −n + 1.

items.q: What is the nth term of −3, −2, −1, 0, …?
items.e: The difference is 1, so start with n. The 1st term of n is 1; to get −3, subtract 4. n − 4.

items.q: What is the nth term of −7, −12, −17, −22, …?
items.e: The difference is −5, so start with −5n. The 1st term of −5n is −5; to get −7, subtract 2. −5n − 2.

items.q: What is the nth term of 5, 17, 29, 41, …?
items.e: The difference is 12, so start with 12n. The 1st term of 12n is 12; to get 5, subtract 7. 12n − 7.

items.q: What is the nth term of −5, −1, 3, 7, …?
items.e: The difference is 4, so start with 4n. The 1st term of 4n is 4; to get −5, subtract 9. 4n − 9.

items.q: What is the nth term of −5, 0, 5, 10, …?
items.e: The difference is 5, so start with 5n. The 1st term of 5n is 5; to get −5, subtract 10. 5n − 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of 0, 12, 24, 36, …?
items.e: The difference is 12, so start with 12n. The 1st term of 12n is 12; to get 0, subtract 12. 12n − 12.

items.q: What is the nth term of −3, 1, 5, 9, …?
items.e: The difference is 4, so start with 4n. The 1st term of 4n is 4; to get −3, subtract 7. 4n − 7.

items.q: What is the nth term of 16, 22, 28, 34, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get 16, add 10. 6n + 10.

items.q: What is the nth term of 4, 7, 10, 13, …?
items.e: The difference is 3, so start with 3n. The 1st term of 3n is 3; to get 4, add 1. 3n + 1.

items.q: What is the nth term of −5, −7, −9, −11, …?
items.e: The difference is −2, so start with −2n. The 1st term of −2n is −2; to get −5, subtract 3. −2n − 3.

items.q: What is the nth term of −9, −13, −17, −21, …?
items.e: The difference is −4, so start with −4n. The 1st term of −4n is −4; to get −9, subtract 5. −4n − 5.

items.q: What is the nth term of 17, 23, 29, 35, …?
items.e: The difference is 6, so start with 6n. The 1st term of 6n is 6; to get 17, add 11. 6n + 11.

items.q: What is the nth term of −3, 5, 13, 21, …?
items.e: The difference is 8, so start with 8n. The 1st term of 8n is 8; to get −3, subtract 11. 8n − 11.

items.q: What is the nth term of 0, −4, −8, −12, …?
items.e: The difference is −4, so start with −4n. The 1st term of −4n is −4; to get 0, add 4. −4n + 4.

items.q: What is the nth term of 5, −2, −9, −16, …?
items.e: The difference is −7, so start with −7n. The 1st term of −7n is −7; to get 5, add 12. −7n + 12.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 320, 160, 80, 40, …
items.e: 40 ÷ 2 = 20. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: The sequence 1, 2, 4, … is geometric. What is the 7th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. The 7th term is 64.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 5th term is 16. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 4 times: 16 ÷ 16 = 1.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 4th term is 8. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 3 times: 8 ÷ 8 = 1.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 3. Its 5th term is 243. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 3 4 times: 243 ÷ 81 = 3.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 3. Its 4th term is 135. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 3 3 times: 135 ÷ 27 = 5.

items.q: The sequence 5, 10, 20, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 2: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80. The 5th term is 80.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 2nd term is 8. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 1 time: 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 160, 80, 40, 20, …
items.e: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 10, −20, 40, −80, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: −20 ÷ 10 = −2.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 128, 64, 32, 16, …
items.e: 16 ÷ 2 = 8. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 4, −8, 16, −32, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: −8 ÷ 4 = −2.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 4th term is 32. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 3 times: 32 ÷ 8 = 4.

items.q: What is the common ratio of 4, 40, 400, 4,000, …?
items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 40 ÷ 4 = 10.

items.q: The sequence 3, 9, 27, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 3, 9, 27, 81, 243. The 5th term is 243.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 3. Its 5th term is 81. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 3 4 times: 81 ÷ 81 = 1.

items.q: The sequence 2, 6, 18, … is geometric. What is the 5th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 3: 2, 6, 18, 54, 162. The 5th term is 162.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 3. Its 3rd term is 45. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 3 2 times: 45 ÷ 9 = 5.

items.q: Each term is the term before divided by 2. What is the next term? 256, 128, 64, 32, …
items.e: 32 ÷ 2 = 16. The common ratio is ½.

items.q: A geometric sequence has common ratio 2. Its 4th term is 16. What is its 1st term?
items.e: Divide by 2 3 times: 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 5, 10, 20, 40, …?
items.e: For a geometric sequence, an = a1 · rn − 1. Here a1 = 5 and r = 2: an = 5 · 2n − 1.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 0, 5, 10, 15, …?
items.e: For an arithmetic sequence, an = a1 + d(n − 1). Here a1 = 0 and d = 5: an = 0 + 5(n − 1).

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 2 and an = 3 · an−1. What is a4?
items.e: Start at 2 and multiply by 3 each time: 2, 6, 18, 54. So a4 = 54.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 8, 11, 14, 17, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = 8; an = an−1 + 3.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence −2, −3, −4, −5, …?
items.e: For an arithmetic sequence, an = a1 + d(n − 1). Here a1 = −2 and d = −1: an = −2 + (−1)(n − 1).

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence −1, −3, −5, −7, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = −1; an = an−1 − 2.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 10, 30, 90, 270, …?
items.e: For a geometric sequence, an = a1 · rn − 1. Here a1 = 10 and r = 3: an = 10 · 3n − 1.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 10, 50, 250, 1,250, …?
items.e: For a geometric sequence, an = a1 · rn − 1. Here a1 = 10 and r = 5: an = 10 · 5n − 1.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 5, 15, 45, 135, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before times 3: a1 = 5; an = 3 · an−1.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 1, −2, 4, −8, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before times −2: a1 = 1; an = (−2) · an−1.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 13, 17, 21, 25, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = 13; an = an−1 + 4.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence −4, 4, 12, 20, …?
items.e: For an arithmetic sequence, an = a1 + d(n − 1). Here a1 = −4 and d = 8: an = −4 + 8(n − 1).

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 5, −10, 20, −40, …?
items.e: Each term is the one before times −2: a1 = 5; an = (−2) · an−1.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 15, 13, 11, 9, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = 15; an = an−1 − 2.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 3 and an = 2 · an−1. What is a5?
items.e: Start at 3 and multiply by 2 each time: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48. So a5 = 48.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 3 and an = (−2) · an−1. What is a4?
items.e: Start at 3 and multiply by −2 each time: 3, −6, 12, −24. So a4 = −24.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 1 and an = an−1 − 4. What is a5?
items.e: Start at 1 and subtract 4 each time: 1, −3, −7, −11, −15. So a5 = −15.

items.q: Which recursive formula gives the sequence 1, −3, −7, −11, …?
items.e: A recursive formula gives the first term and how to get each term from the one before: a1 = 1; an = an−1 − 4.

items.q: A sequence is defined by a1 = 13 and an = an−1 + 1. What is a5?
items.e: Start at 13 and add 1 each time: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. So a5 = 17.

items.q: Which explicit formula gives the sequence 3, 15, 75, 375, …?
items.e: For a geometric sequence, an = a1 · rn − 1. Here a1 = 3 and r = 5: an = 3 · 5n − 1.

items.q: What is the next term of the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
items.e: Add the two terms before: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: A geometric sequence has a1 = 5 and r = 2. Which is a8?
What is the next triangular number? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
items.e: The differences go up by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, so add 6: 21.

items.q: A theater has 20 seats in row 1, 23 in row 2, 26 in row 3, and so on. How many seats are in row 15?
A bacteria population doubles every hour. It starts at 50. How many are there after 5 hours?
items.e: 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1,600. This is a geometric sequence with ratio 2.

items.q: Grace saves $5 in week 1, $8 in week 2, $11 in week 3, and so on. How much does she save in week 10?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 2. Week 10: 3 × 10 + 2 = $32.

items.q: A ball is dropped from 200 cm. Each bounce reaches half the height of the one before. How high is the 3rd bounce?
Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. How many sticks are in pattern 20?
items.e: The nth term is 3n + 1. Pattern 20: 3 × 20 + 1 = 61.

items.q: Patterns are made from sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, … sticks. Which pattern uses 100 sticks?
The nth term of a sequence is 50 − 4n. What is the first negative term?
Which sequence has the nth term 5 − 2n?
A car worth $16,000 loses half its value every 3 years. What is it worth after 9 years?
Find the missing term in the geometric sequence 3, ☐, 75, 375, …
items.e: The ratio is 375 ÷ 75 = 5, so 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: Find the missing term in the arithmetic sequence 7, ☐, 19, 25, …
items.e: The difference is 6, so 7 + 6 = 13.

items.q: Which is the nth term of 2, 4, 8, 16, …?
items.e: Each term is a power of 2: 21, 22, 23, … so the nth term is 2n.

items.q: Which is the nth term of 1, 4, 9, 16, …?
items.e: These are the square numbers: n2.

items.q: Ethan says 2, 6, 18, 54, … is arithmetic because the numbers go up. Is he right?
c: No, it is geometric with ratio 3
items.e: The differences are 4, 12, 36, which are not equal. Each term is × 3: geometric with ratio 3.

items.q: The 5th term of an arithmetic sequence is 23 and the 6th term is 27. What is the 1st term?
items.e: The difference is 4. Go back 4 steps from the 5th term: 23 − 16 = 7.

items.q: A sequence starts 3, 7, and each term is twice the term before minus 1. What is the 4th term?
How many terms of 7, 11, 15, 19, … are less than 100?
items.e: The nth term is 4n + 3. 4n + 3 < 100 when n < 24.25, so 24 terms.
